text: The authors of the misleading answers wrote the corresponding intended critiques, checked whether other labelers in the assistance experiment found them, and judged whether each new critique was valid. The paper reports assisted labelers found the intended critique 45 ± 5% of the time versus 27 ± 5% without assistance; the fraction of critiques judged valid did not appreciably decrease (71% vs 73%), while the number of valid critiques was much higher (0.96 vs 0.62) and valid novel critiques rose (0.24 vs 0.18).
title: Misleading answers: assisted labelers find intended critiques 45% vs 27% unassisted
